title: SPE Chapter 02 — Styled
_comment: VET THIS FILE before rendering. Each scene = one short narration beat (aim 5-10s) + one visual. lane 'app' shows the running page at app-relative path (optional 'js' runs the app's Base API after load: pin sidebars, set scheme, toggle theme, toast — state persists across the run). lane 'code' shows the native GitHub blob with lines hl highlighted. Rebuild: RESYNTH=1 bash scripts/make-episode.sh 02-Styled

scenes.narr: Chapter two takes the exact three pages from chapter one and dresses them in a complete application shell.
A bar across the top, a navigation panel on the left, and a settings panel on the right — and every pixel of that comes from shared CSS, not from the PHP.
The settings panel restyles the whole page on the fly. This is the Ocean scheme.
And this is Forest — four schemes in all, each of them just a single class set on the root element.
It also flips between light and dark, and your choice is remembered in local storage for the next visit.
Back to light, and notice the layout never moved through any of that — only the colours changed.
The remarkable part is the PHP, because it barely changed. This is still a single echo of a single anonymous class, exactly as before.
The pages constant now pairs each page with an icon name, ready to become links in the navigation sidebar.
A second constant lists the four colour schemes, again just an icon and a label for each one.
The request selects a page exactly as it did before, and a match expression returns that page's content, or a clean 404 for anything unknown.
The navigation links are built with the pipe operator, mapping every page to an anchor and marking the current one as active.
And the entire shell — the top bar, both panels, and the main area — is one heredoc of plain HTML, with no templating engine in sight.
It pulls in three shared files — the base styles, the site theme, and the script that runs the sidebars and themes — and every later chapter reuses exactly these.
The About page makes the lesson concrete: moving between pages swaps only the content, while the shell around it stays put.
Contact is a plain mailto link with no JavaScript at all — a form the server genuinely receives waits until chapter six.
And small flourishes, like this toast notification, are a single shared JavaScript call.
That is chapter two: the very same engine, now presentable. Next, chapter three introduces plugins, and the code finally begins to grow.
